text:
morgan: FYI, saw two OOM incidents on shard-7 this morning during long-context chat sessions (~45k-60k tokens). They correlate with KV cache growth + high fragmentation.
jamal: logs? any repro?
morgan: extracting main bits. stack shows KV alloc failures after a long run: 
```
[2026-03-17T03:12:10Z] ERROR runtime/kvcache: alloc failed: requested 8192 pages, available 0
[2026-03-17T03:12:10Z] ERROR runtime/serving: request_id=... oom while preparing kv for gen step
[2026-03-17T03:12:10Z] WARN runtime/kvcache: fragmentation: free_regions=3 sizes=[128k,64k,32k] total_free=224k but largest_fit<needed
```
lee: that fragmentation line is the red flag. We saw similar symptoms when kernel selection started favoring the new fused-attn path that allocates large temporary buffers and delays reclaim.
sophia: repro steps?
morgan: quick repro on dev with a single client streaming a 60k token prompt. command: 
```bash
# reproduce long context growth
run_load --model rwd-llama-13b --context 60000 --stream 1 --concurrency 1 --profile kv,mem
```
and profiler output: 
```
KVCacheSize: 3.8GB -> 6.1GB over 45k tokens
PagesAllocated: +1.9M
CompactCalls: 0
Evictions: 2 (both full-page evictions, heavy IO)
```
jamal: why 0 compacts? we have compact-on-threshold set to 0.7 right? maybe not firing because fragmentation metric is wrong.
lee: hypothesis: batching heuristics changed last week to hold onto more KV pages for reuse across batches (to reduce recompute) but we didn't tighten the upper soft-quota. Combined with fused kernel's temporary buffers, we overshoot mem and evictions are expensive -> fragmentation spikes.
sophia: short-term mitigations we can push: reduce batching window, enable aggressive compaction, add soft quota check pre-alloc. Proposed config patch: 
```yaml
kv:
  soft_quota_fraction: 0.6
  compaction_enabled: true
  compaction_min_free_ratio: 0.12
  early_evict_on_alloc_fail: true
batching:
  max_window_ms: 10  # down from 50
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
```
morgan: +1 to that. Also add a graceful fallback: if mem estimate > 0.8 total, route to small-model variant automatically or switch to truncated context path that 1) flushes older KV pages and 2) signals client about truncation.
jamal: do we have a mem-estimate function exposed in router? we can do preflight estimates based on active kv_size + incoming tokens * per-token-kv.
sophia: yes, router has approximate_kv_bytes(model, tokens). I'll add a preflight check that returns HTTP 429-like with header X-Redwood-Fallback: truncation or model-space or lowers batch concurrency.
lee: also implement an async background compacter that runs when fragmentation > threshold for > 30s (avoid thrash). And add `kv_reuse_age` so we expire very old prefix pages earlier.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042. Assigned: oncall-engineering. Playbook link: https://ret.internal/incidents/INC-2026-042
morgan: for rollback: temporary knob we can flip: disable fused-attn kernel selection for long-context routes (kernel_selection.long_context_preference=false) — that avoids the big temporaries while we tune kv heuristics.
jamal: agreed. also adding a retry strategy at request layer: on alloc failure, do up to 2 soft-retries where we force a compact and reduce batch window by 2x, then retry. That should avoid hard failure in most cases.
sophia: sample patch for retry pseudo: 
```py
def serve_request(req):
  for attempt in range(3):
    if estimate_mem(req) > soft_limit:
      apply_graceful_fallback(req)
      return fallback_response
    try:
      process(req)
      return resp
    except KVAllocError:
      if attempt < 2:
        compact_kv_shard(req.shard)
        reduce_batching(req.route)
        sleep(0.05)
        continue
      else:
        raise
```
lee: metrics we should add now: per-shard fragmentation_ratio, largest_free_block_bytes, kv_reuse_hit_ratio, compaction_time_ms, preflight_mem_est_percent. Dashboards and an alert when fragmentation_ratio > 0.4 for 2m.
morgan: timeline: patch compaction + soft quota + router preflight + retry logic -> test in staging today, rollout to canary tomorrow, full rollout after 24h. I'll open PRs and link here.
jamal: also run a synthetic long-context soak for 12h to measure growth and fragmentation under the new configs. Use a mixture of prompt lengths and checkpoint rerefs.
sophia: noted. I'll own running the soak and the dashboard.
morgan: thanks. if anyone sees spikes tonight ping #oncall. I'll monitor the canary. :thumbsup:
